description: Replace stage 3 hard threshold with soft-attention assignment annealed via temperature scheduler
papers: 1:HILL — Hierarchical Index Learning for Foundation Retrieval Models (Meta Ads, arXiv 2604.12965v1)
steps: Add scale.soft_cluster.assign_soft(embeddings, centroids, alpha) returning per-tool softmax distribution over centroids and a pseudo-centroid c_bar = sum_k a_k c_k
Implement temperature schedule alpha = max_alpha * (iter / max_iters)^exp over stage-3 refinement iterations
Add a balance regularizer term penalizing assignment-mass collapse (FLOPs-style) during centroid refresh
Expose config flag soft_cluster=True that routes stage 3 through the new path; default False preserves current behavior
Unit test on 9-tool fixture: with default alpha schedule must converge to clustering within tolerance of current hard clustering
Unit test low-alpha case: assignment entropy above threshold (non-trivial overlap between groups)
Integration test on 1k synthetic catalog: balance regularizer reduces stddev of cluster sizes by at least 30 percent vs no-regularizer baseline
refers: 0::0::HILL Algorithm 1 'One-Layer Attention Learning' uses soft assignment a_k = softmax(-alpha * d(j,k)) over learnable index-node centroids c_k, producing pseudo embedding c_bar = sum_k a_k c_k; we mirror this for tool-to-group assignment so cluster boundaries are differentiable rather than threshold-snapped

1::0::HILL Section 3.3 'softmax temperature scheduler' alpha = max_alpha * (current_iter^exp / max_iters^exp) starts loose and sharpens; fixes our 'all singletons or one giant cluster' knife-edge at small scale
2::0::HILL Section 3.3 'FLOPs regularizer / Balanced Index Distribution' penalizes collapse of assignment mass to few clusters; replaces our post-hoc rebalance.py fix-up
3::0::HILL paper opts-in joint training via end-to-end loss; we cannot differentiate our LLM labeler so we keep the mechanism opt-in and offline-only

description: Stage 4 clusters on residual = embedding - parent_centroid so deeper levels capture finer detail
papers: 1:HILL — Hierarchical Index Learning for Foundation Retrieval Models (Meta Ads, arXiv 2604.12965v1)
steps: Add scale.residual_cluster.cluster_upward_residual(level_n_nodes, parent_centroids) that subtracts each node's parent centroid before calling existing cluster_upward
Wire reconstruction invariant: sum of centroids on a leaf's root-to-leaf path approximates the leaf embedding within epsilon
Expose config flag residual_upward=True; default False
Unit test reconstruction invariant on 9-tool fixture: for every leaf ||sum(path centroids) - leaf_embedding|| < epsilon
Unit test residual math: cluster_upward_residual output on pre-centered input equals cluster_upward output on raw input
Integration test on 1k synthetic: L2 discriminability score improves vs non-residual baseline
refers: 0::0::HILL Section 3.4 'Cross-Layer Residual Learning' inspired by residual quantization: r_j^n = r_j^{n-1} - c_bar_j^{n-1}; coarse layers capture general concepts, deeper layers capture fine detail
1::0::HILL reconstruction loss sum_j ||q_j^N - v||^2 ensures cumulative path approximates original embedding; we adopt this as a stage-4 sanity invariant rather than a training loss
2::0::HILL treats residual learning as an opt-in mechanism layered on top of the base clustering stack; default-off keeps behavior stable until validated

description: Phase 2 feedback emits per-level positive labels by walking the routing path, not just the final tool
papers: 1:HILL — Hierarchical Index Learning for Foundation Retrieval Models (Meta Ads, arXiv 2604.12965v1)
steps: Extend retrieval.traverser to return the descended path (list of node_ids from root to leaf-parent) alongside tool_ids
Populate RouteRecord.path in router.service with the returned path — the field already exists but is emitted empty today
Extend feedback.heuristics: when leaf label is POSITIVE, emit one FeedbackRecord per (level, node) on the path
Apply graduated confidence floor by level: L1 conf>=0.4, L2 conf>=0.6, L3 conf>=0.8 (deeper levels demand more certainty)
Extend rebuild.eval_adapter to read per-level labels and pass to autotune as level-stratified eval sets
Unit test on synthetic session log: a positive leaf produces N labels where N = path depth; confidences match graduated schedule
Integration test: autotune receives distinct per-level eval sets and picks different winning configs per level
refers: 0::0::HILL Section 3.5 beam-search traversal records the full root-to-leaf path; we mirror this by having the traverser return the descended node_ids alongside the final tool_ids
1::0::HILL training data is <user, intermediate-node> pairs materialized from path traces — requires the route path to be persisted at serving time
2::0::HILL Section 3.5 'Test-time training data extraction' walks beam-search paths from leaf to root and harvests <user, intermediate index node> pairs; we do the same from telemetry paths
3::0::HILL filters phi_DEP and phi_IR(u, i^n) = |Int(u,n-1) intersect Child(i^n)| / |Child(i^n)| keep only precise pairs; we translate to per-level confidence floors
3::0::HILL Table reports best Gowalla result with phi_DEP=2, phi_IR=0.8 at L2 and 0.4 at L3 — confirming graduated strictness
4::0::HILL trains a separate model per level using the harvested per-level pairs; our autotune consumes them as level-stratified eval sets for the same effect

description: Use heavier LLM at L1/L2 (few high-stakes decisions) and cheaper LLM at L3 (many decisions)
papers: 1:HILL — Hierarchical Index Learning for Foundation Retrieval Models (Meta Ads, arXiv 2604.12965v1)
steps: Extend Config.labeler_llm from a single provider to optional per-level dict {L1: opus, L2: sonnet, L3: haiku}
Keep backward compatibility: a single LLMProvider still works unchanged
Add _select_llm(node.level) helper in labeling/describe.py — no prompt changes
Propagate the same per-level mapping to config.loader YAML parsing
Unit test: single-provider config routes every level to the same provider (backward compat)
Unit test: per-level config dispatches correctly by node.level
Cost report on 1k synthetic catalog: total LLM spend drops at least 50 percent vs single-Opus baseline with recall@10 delta within 2 percent
refers: 0::0::HILL Section 4 Stacked MoNN deployment uses 2-3 layers (L1 coarse / L3 fine) with different model complexities per granularity
1::0::HILL keeps single-model deployment as a valid degenerate case of the stack; backward-compat with a single LLMProvider preserves this
2::0::HILL per-level model dispatch is a routing decision driven solely by tree level, not content — matches a simple _select_llm(level) helper
3::0::HILL configuration treats the per-level stack as deployment policy, not model architecture; YAML-level configurability mirrors that operational stance
6::0::HILL results: 2-Layer MoNN (Large+Small) achieves -0.97 percent NE and +6.0 percent Recall at only 3.9x cost vs MoNN Large at 24.6x — same-quality, cheaper deployment

description: After initial clustering, run K iterations of FAISS K-Means as an EM-style refinement step
papers: 1:HILL — Hierarchical Index Learning for Foundation Retrieval Models (Meta Ads, arXiv 2604.12965v1)
steps: Extend scale.ann_neighbors with build_kmeans_centroids(embeddings, n_clusters, n_iter) wrapping faiss.Kmeans (numpy fallback when faiss unavailable)
Add EM refinement loop after stage 3: E-step reassigns tools to nearest current centroid; M-step recomputes centroids; iterate to convergence or max_iter
Expose config flag em_refine_iters (default 0 = disabled)
Unit test convergence: within-cluster sum-of-squares decreases monotonically per iteration on synthetic data
Unit test fallback: numpy path matches faiss path within tolerance on small inputs
Integration test on 1k synthetic: 5 EM iterations reduce WCSS by at least 10 percent vs no refinement
refers: 0::0::HILL Section 3.6 uses FAISS GPU K-Means as the core centroid primitive; we wrap faiss.Kmeans with a numpy fallback to keep the same interface
1::0::HILL Section 3.6 'EM approximation via FAISS' treats indices as Gaussian-mixture clusters — E-step assigns with GPU K-Means, M-step updates model
2::0::HILL treats EM iteration count as a tuning knob; default-off (em_refine_iters=0) preserves pre-refinement behavior until opted in
5::0::HILL ablation shows EM-HILL within ~0.04 percent NE of full HILL — near-free quality with simpler infra

description: Multi-vector inner-node scoring in retrieve(): score = max(cos(query, node.embedding), max over child.embedding). Recovers recall lost when an inner node's description is too broad to discriminate against siblings.
papers: 1:ColBERT — Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT (Khattab and Zaharia, arXiv 2004.12832)
2:HILL — Hierarchical Index Learning for Foundation Retrieval Models (Meta Ads, arXiv 2604.12965v1) Section 3.2
steps: Add _node_score(tree, node, query) helper in retrieval/traverser.py: max of node.embedding cosine and each inner-child cosine
Replace the two -_cos(n.embedding, query_embedding) sort keys in retrieve() and retrieve_with_path() with -_node_score(tree, n, query_embedding)
Leaf-parent step keeps using the parent's own embedding for tool-score collection (do not multi-vectorize the leaf step — that is Direction 1's job)
Add unit test: a tree where a node's description embedding is far from query but one child is close — assert the node now wins the frontier
Add unit test: empty children list falls back to node.embedding cosine (no regression for leaf-parent groups)
Re-run scripts/stage_validate.py --run raw-tools and assert recall@10 >= 0.97 (baseline 0.917 -> measured 0.978)
refers: 0::0::ColBERT introduces MaxSim over multi-vectors as the scoring rule for late interaction — we apply the same operator at the inner-node level instead of the token level

1::1::HILL Section 3.2 soft-attention clustering produces per-node mixture distributions over children; this task is the simplest realization of that idea (use the existing child embeddings as the mixture)
5::0::Empirical recall lift on raw-tools eval set: 0.917 -> 0.978 (+0.061), with errors stable at 4 and warnings dropping 28 -> 20

description: ColBERT-style leaf reranker: pull top-2k tools from the traverser, rerank to top-k by MaxSim between query and per-tool multi-vectors (intent_phrase + each example_query). Stacks additively on Direction 3.
papers: 1:ColBERT — Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT (Khattab and Zaharia, arXiv 2004.12832)
steps: Add retrieval/rerank.py with rerank_tools(query_emb, candidates, tool_vectors_by_id) -> ranked tool ids using MaxSim
Pre-embed each tool's intent_phrase + example_queries once at startup; persist via the existing DiskCache so warm starts are free
Extend retrieve() with rerank_k parameter (default = k); when rerank_k > k, pull rerank_k candidates and apply rerank_tools
Wire validation/recall_benchmark.py to accept rerank_k; default keeps current behavior
Add unit test: a tool whose intent_phrase embedding is far from query but one of its example_query embeddings is close — assert reranker promotes it
Re-run validate stacked on Direction 3; assert recall@10 >= 0.99 (measured 0.994 = 179/180 hits)
refers: 0::0::ColBERT scores documents by sum-of-max cosines between query token vectors and document token vectors; we use the same MaxSim operator with sentence-level vectors (intent_phrase plus example_queries) as the document's multi-vector representation
5::0::Empirical recall lift on raw-tools stacked on Direction 3: 0.978 -> 0.994 (+0.016 stacking gain, +0.077 cumulative vs v7)
